\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{વીમો} (vīmo)}{વીમો (vīmo)}]{\gu{વીમો} (vīmo) — insurance}

\label{lesson:GU-C372-vimo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a debt, then the Gujarati for to lose for good.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{વીમો}}
\textbf{\gu{વીમો}} — \emph{vīmo} — \textquotedblleft{}insurance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{ગાડીનો} \gu{વીમો} \gu{હશે} \gu{તો} \gu{મરામતના} \gu{પૈસા} \gu{બચશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo gāḍīno vīmo haśe to marāmatnā paisā bacśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the car is insured, you will save on repairs.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{વીમો}} (\emph{vīmo}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bīma}, \textquotedblleft{}fear; insurance\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vīmo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vīmo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo gāḍīno vīmo haśe to marāmatnā paisā bacśe.} — If the car is insured, you will save on repairs.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a debt, then the Gujarati for to lose for good, then say \emph{vīmo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{વીમો} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Insurance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ગેરંટી} (geranṭī)}{ગેરંટી (geranṭī)}]{\gu{ગેરંટી} (geranṭī) — a guarantee}

\label{lesson:GU-C372-geranti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to lose for good, then the Gujarati for insurance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ગેરંટી}}
\textbf{\gu{ગેરંટી}} — \emph{geranṭī} — \textquotedblleft{}a guarantee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{પંખો} \gu{બગડશે} \gu{તો} \gu{દુકાનદાર} \gu{ગેરંટીને} \gu{લીધે} \gu{તેને} \gu{મફત} \gu{સુધારશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo paṅkho bagaḍśe to dukāndār geranṭīne līdhe tene maphat sudhārśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the fan breaks down, the shopkeeper will repair it free under the guarantee.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ગેરંટી}} (\emph{geranṭī}) is borrowed from English \emph{guarantee}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{geranṭī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo paṅkho bagaḍśe to dukāndār geranṭīne līdhe tene maphat sudhārśe.} — If the fan breaks down, the shopkeeper will repair it free under the guarantee.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to lose for good, then the Gujarati for insurance, then say \emph{geranṭī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{કવચ} (kavac)}{કવચ (kavac)}]{\gu{કવચ} (kavac) — a protective cover; armour}

\label{lesson:GU-C372-kavac}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for insurance, then the Gujarati for a guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{કવચ}}
\textbf{\gu{કવચ}} — \emph{kavac} — \textquotedblleft{}a protective cover; armour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{ઘર} \gu{પર} \gu{વીમાનું} \gu{કવચ} \gu{હશે} \gu{તો} \gu{આગ} \gu{પછી} \gu{મરામતની} \gu{ચિંતા} \gu{નહીં} \gu{રહે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo ghar par vīmānũ kavac haśe to āg pachī marāmatnī cintā nahī̃ rahe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the house has insurance cover, there will be no worry about repairs after a fire.
\end{quote}

A neuter noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{કવચ}} (\emph{kavac}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{kavaca}, \textquotedblleft{}armour, a coat of mail; any covering\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): what covers and guards.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kavac}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kavac}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo ghar par vīmānũ kavac haśe to āg pachī marāmatnī cintā nahī̃ rahe.} — If the house has insurance cover, there will be no worry about repairs after a fire.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for insurance, then the Gujarati for a guarantee, then say \emph{kavac} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સચેત} (sacet)}{સચેત (sacet)}]{\gu{સચેત} (sacet) — alert}

\label{lesson:GU-C372-sacet}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a guarantee, then the Gujarati for a protective cover.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સચેત}}
\textbf{\gu{સચેત}} — \emph{sacet} — \textquotedblleft{}alert\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ભીડમાં} \gu{સચેત} \gu{રહો}, \gu{નહીંતર} \gu{પાકીટ} \gu{ખોવાઈ} \gu{જશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhīḍmā̃ sacet raho, nahī̃tar pākīṭ khovāī jaśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Stay alert in the crowd, or you will lose your wallet.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સચેત}} (\emph{sacet}) is usually traced to Sanskrit \emph{sacetas}, \textquotedblleft{}conscious, intelligent\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), built from \emph{sa-}, \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{cetas}, \textquotedblleft{}mind\textquotedblright{}: with one's mind awake to what goes on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sacet}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sacet}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhīḍmā̃ sacet raho, nahī̃tar pākīṭ khovāī jaśe.} — Stay alert in the crowd, or you will lose your wallet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a guarantee, then the Gujarati for a protective cover, then say \emph{sacet} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{આવરવું} (āvarvũ)}{આવરવું (āvarvũ)}]{\gu{આવરવું} (āvarvũ) — to include}

\label{lesson:GU-C372-avarvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a protective cover, then the Gujarati for alert.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{આવરવું}}
\textbf{\gu{આવરવું}} — \emph{āvarvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to include\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{આ} \gu{વીમો} \gu{આગ} \gu{અને} \gu{પૂર} \gu{બંનેને} \gu{આવરશે} \gu{તો} \gu{હું} \gu{તે} \gu{લઈશ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo ā vīmo āg ane pūr bannene āvarśe to hũ te laīś.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this policy covers both fire and flood, I will take it.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{બધા} \gu{પ્રશ્નો} \gu{આવર્યા}, \emph{teṇe badhā praśno āvaryā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{આવરવું}} (\emph{āvarvũ}) CDIAL lists the Gujarati verb, \textquotedblleft{}to cover, to spread over\textquotedblright{}, under a reconstructed \emph{āvarati}, \textquotedblleft{}covers\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1414).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a protective cover, then the Gujarati for alert, then say \emph{āvarvũ} again
\end{itemize}
